item.title: The best early Black Friday deals you can already shop
item.description:
The countdown to Black Friday is on, and the discounts are starting to appear. Although the shopping holiday isn’t officially until November 27th, retailers are already dropping early deals on some of our favorite tech. Of course, with prices rising across the board, a good discount doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting a historically low price. But we’re still seeing worthwhile discounts on a host of tried-and-tested gear, with more expected next week.

Below, we’ve rounded up the best early Black Friday deals we’ve found so far. Prices could drop further as Black Friday approaches, as is always the case, but these deals are worth considering if you’d rather shop early and beat the holiday rush. We’ll continue to update this guide as more retailers launch their holiday sales, too, so be sure to check back regularly as we get closer to the main event.

AirPods Pro 3

Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $249 $179 at Amazon
  • $249 $179 at Walmart
  • $249 $179.99 at Best Buy

Sony DualSense Wireless Controller

Sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.

Where to Buy:

  • $74.99 $54 at Amazon
  • $74.99 $54.99 at Best Buy
  • $74.99 $54.99 at Target

007 First Light

007 First Light, a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman, is arguably the best action game we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $69.99 $34.99 at PlayStation Store

Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus

Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.

Where to Buy:

  • $69.99 $29.99 at Amazon
  • $69.99 $29.99 at Best Buy

Apple Watch Series 12

The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $399 $329 at Amazon
  • $399 $329 at Walmart
  • $399 $329 at Best Buy

Philips Hue Essential four-pack of bulbs

Philips Hue bulbs can be pricey, which is why the company’s four-pack of Essential A19 bulbs is a great buy at the current sale price. The adjustable bulbs offer white and color ambiance, 800 lumens of brightness, and can be controlled either via Bluetooth or a Hue Bridge (sold separately).

Where to Buy:

  • $59.99 $41.99 at Amazon (four-pack)
  • $119.99 $99.99 at Best Buy (with Hue Bridge)
  • $119.99 $97.99 at Amazon (with Hue Bridge)

Fanttik S1 Pro Cordless Electric Screwdriver

Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.

Where to Buy:

  • $79.99 $39.99 at Amazon

Nothing Ear 3A earbuds

You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $99 $69 at Amazon
  • $99 $69 at Walmart
  • $99 $69 at Best Buy

MacBook Neo

Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $799 $749 at Amazon (512GB)
  • $699 $649 at Best Buy (256GB)
  • $699 $649 at Amazon (256GB)

Bose SoundLink Max SE speaker

The cheaper, more streamlined SoundLink Max features a slightly smaller battery (16 vs. 20 hours) and lacks external power bank functionality. Otherwise, it’s the same as the standard model, which means the audio is just as great.

Where to Buy:

  • $349 $229 at Best Buy

Ember Mug 3 (14-ounce)

Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.

Where to Buy:

  • $149.95 $99.99 at Amazon
  • $149.95 $99.99 at Best Buy
  • $149.95 $99.99 at Ember

LG B6E OLED TV

Despite being an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, this model features four HDMI 2.1 ports, a 120Hz refresh rate, a capable processor, and pixel-perfect image quality and contrast for any content you want to watch. Lower brightness is likely the biggest compromise with getting a cheaper OLED.

Where to Buy:

  • $1399.99 $799.99 at Best Buy (55-inch)
  • $1899.99 $999.99 at Best Buy (65-inch)
  • $2699.99 $1499.99 at Best Buy (77-inch)

JBL Tour One M3

JBL’s Tour One M3 noise-canceling headphones come with a touchscreen-equipped wireless transmitter that lets you wirelessly listen to audio from in-flight entertainment systems and other devices without Bluetooth. They also offer solid active noise cancellation and last up to 70 hours on a charge.

Where to Buy:

  • $449.95 $149.95 at Amazon
  • $449.95 $149.95 at Best Buy
  • $449.95 $149.95 at JBL

Hisense CanvasTV (2026)

Hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.

Where to Buy:

  • $1499.99 $697.99 at Amazon (55-inch)
  • $1499.99 $699.99 at Best Buy (55-inch)
  • $1999.99 $897.99 at Amazon (65-inch)

Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo

The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is a beginner-friendly 3D printer that supports four filament spools. It features an enclosed build chamber, automatic bed leveling, and a large touchscreen, making it easy to produce reliable prints.

Where to Buy:

  • $449 $369 at Elegoo

Moft Trackable Tripod Wallet

Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.

Where to Buy:

  • $59.99 $50.99 at Amazon
  • $59.99 $50.99 at Moft

Govee Table Lamp 2

Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.

Where to Buy:

  • $79.99 $63.99 at Amazon
  • $79.99 $63.99 at Govee

Birdfy Feeder Metal 2 4K

Birdfy’s metal smart bird feeder features a wide-angle 4K camera that lets you get an up-close look at visiting birds, along with a 1.8-liter seed capacity and a built-in solar panel for charging. It also offers free AI-powered recognition of more than 6,000 bird species.

Where to Buy:

  • $279.99 $219.99 at Amazon
  • $279.99 $199.99 at Birdfy

Tessan Voyager 205 Universal Travel Adapter

Tessan’s universal travel adapter delivers up to 205W of combined USB charging power and can charge up to eight devices, including a pair of laptops, at the same time. It features six USB-C ports, including two that can deliver up to 140W individually, a USB-A port, and an AC outlet. It also works in over 200 countries and regions.

Where to Buy:

  • $128 $89 at Tessan (with code TSWTA13S)

Bambu Lab P2S Combo

Bambu Lab’s P2S Combo is a 3D printer that can print in multiple colors and automatically dry its materials to help improve print quality. It also features a 5-inch touchscreen, a built-in camera for monitoring prints remotely, and AI-powered tools that can detect printing problems.

Where to Buy:

  • $749.99 $649.99 at Best Buy
  • $749 $649 at Bambu Lab

Eight Sleep Pod 6

Eight Sleep’s Pod 6 automatically adjusts your bed’s temperature based on your sleep patterns, heart rate, and breathing. It features a redesigned hub that’s half the size of its predecessor and adjusts temperatures faster. The system also tracks sleep quality, detects snoring, and lets couples control the temperature on each side of the bed independently.

Where to Buy:

  • $2899 $2699 at Eight Sleep

Flextail Zero Pump 2

Flextail’s Zero Pump 2 might weigh a mere 1.7 ounces, but it can quickly inflate and deflate a sleeping pad. It comes with six nozzles and a replaceable battery that recharges via USB-C, allowing you to inflate up to 30 pads on a single charge.

Where to Buy:

  • $56.99 $50.15 at Flextail (with code BF12)

Litter-Robot 4 Starter Bundle

The last-gen Litter-Robot 4 can monitor your cat’s visits, track their weight, and automatically separate waste from clean litter after each use, so you can go up to eight days without emptying your cat’s litter box. The so-called starter bundle also includes 20 pounds of litter, 25 waste drawer liners, a host of odor-control accessories, a litter-trapping mat, and a three-year warranty.

Where to Buy:

  • $963 $813 at Whisker

Headspace subscription

Headspace makes it easier to build mindfulness into your everyday life, whether you’re looking to manage stress, improve focus, or get a better night’s sleep. An annual subscription gives you access to hundreds of guided meditations, breathing exercises, and other tools for beginners and experienced users alike.

Where to Buy:

  • $69.99 $34.99 at Headspace (12 months)

Casetify Moonaries illo Edition 2 phone case

Part of Casetify’s early Black Friday sale, which offers up to 50 percent off select phone case styles, this Moonaries Illo case features playful artwork from the illustrator behind Mocha Cat. It’s available for the iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro, and other iPhone models.

Where to Buy:

  • $100 $45 at Casetify

Sharge Icemag 3 Power Bank

The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.

Where to Buy:

  • $79.9 $69.9 at Amazon (black, with Prime)
  • $79.9 $69.9 at Amazon (white, with Prime)
  • $79.9 $67.9 at Sharge

Ecoflow Laptop Power Bank

EcoFlow’s 25,000mAh / 90Wh battery laptop power bank can deliver up to 140W of power through either of its two USB-C ports, or a combined 170W when charging up to three devices simultaneously. The TSA-approved battery also features a built-in display for monitoring power output.

Where to Buy:

  • $85.79 $46.49 at Amazon

Saros

Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $69.99 $39.99 at Amazon
  • $69.99 $39.99 at Best Buy
  • $69.99 $39.89 at PlayStation Store

Bose QuietComfort Headphones Gen 2

Bose’s second-gen QuietComfort Headphones build on the original with better sound quality and support for lossless audio over USB-C. They also offer improved noise cancellation and are more comfortable thanks to their lack of “eardrum suck.”

Where to Buy:

  • $359 $199 at Amazon
  • $359 $199 at Best Buy
  • $359 $199 at Bose

Garmin Forerunner 265S

Garmin’s midrange Forerunner watch has an OLED display, a week’s worth of battery life, and dual-frequency GPS for better accuracy. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $449.99 $299.99 at Amazon
  • $449.99 $299.99 at Best Buy
  • $449.99 $299.99 at Garmin

Dreame X60 Ultra

The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets, thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.

Where to Buy:

  • $1499.99 $999.99 at Amazon
  • $1499.99 $1059.99 at Best Buy (with Dreame W10 vacuum)
  • $1499.99 $999.99 at Dreame

Matic robot vacuum

The Matic robot vacuum and mop is ideal for cluttered homes with pets, multiple floors, and a mixture of carpets and hardwood. It offers almost human-like navigation, tackling high-pile rugs, and mopping up wet spills. The quiet bot also requires less maintenance than many rivals thanks to its onboard water tank and dust bag. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $1795 $1495 at Matic (Standard Bundle)
  • $1995 $1595 at Matic (Serene Bundle)

Eufy Omni C28

The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.

Where to Buy:

  • $799.99 $459.99 at Amazon
  • $799.99 $459.99 at Eufy (with code WS24C28200NEW1)

Nothing Headphone 1

Nothing’s first pair of over-ear headphones feature a retro transparent design and high-end features like active noise cancellation, spatial audio with head tracking, and plush ear pads. They also feature a paddle button that allows you to control music playback. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $299 $169 at Amazon
  • $299 $169 at Nothing

Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro

Amazon’s 12.3-inch Alexa Tablet 12 Pro runs Android with access to the Google Play Store, unlike the company’s Fire tablets. It also features built-in Alexa Plus integration, a dedicated Kindle reading mode, and up to 16 hours of battery life. Read our hands-on impressions.

Where to Buy:

  • $549.99 $399.99 at Amazon
  • $549.99 $399.99 at Best Buy

Samsung The Frame (2025)

Samsung’s last-gen Frame is a 4K QLED TV that displays art on its anti-glare matte screen when not in use. It also supports Dolby Atmos, HDR10 Plus, and popular streaming apps, with refresh rates up to 144Hz on larger models.

Where to Buy:

  • $899.99 $697.99 at Amazon (55-inch)
  • $899.99 $699.99 at Best Buy (55-inch)

TP-Link Tapo Matter-Certified Smart Plug Mini

TP-Link’s smart smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms, and lets you set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.

Where to Buy:

  • $19.99 $7.99 at Amazon
  • $23.99 $14.99 at Amazon (two-pack)

Update, November 18th: Added a host of new deals, including those for the Apple Watch Series 12, 007 Fire Light, and the Matic robot vacuum.

item.title: What is Nvidia without AI’s sugar daddy in charge?
item.description:
If the glorious AI revolution rests entirely on the well-being of one man, AI is perhaps not as robust a technology as I had previously been led to believe. Nonetheless, chunks of Silicon Valley are now insisting he is indispensable. For instance, if Elon Musk is telling the truth, then Jensen Huang (the former CEO of Nvidia, a company with a market cap of about $3 trillion) has been making deals that were "a handshake with Jensen" with suppliers - "not a written contract," Musk wrote.

Fascinating stuff to tell shareholders. But after listening to Nvidia's first earnings call with its new CEO, Colette Kress, I do think something may have sh …

Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Our favorite accessories to level up your gaming setup ahead of GTA VI
item.description:
With Grand Theft Auto VI set to finally launch tomorrow, November 19th, our long-awaited return to Vice City is nearly here. But after all this time, some of the gear you’ve used in San Andreas might feel out of place on the glamorous streets of Leonidas County. Luckily for you, we’ve gathered a few of our favorite Xbox and PlayStation 5 accessories to help your long gaming sessions run as smoothly as possible.

Controllers

The 8BitDo Ultimate 3E — an upgraded pick for Xbox Series X and Series S consoles — is a very capable, comfortable controller with elite-level features, including a high polling rate and adjustable triggers. It’s on the expensive side at $149.99, but the customization and clean execution justify the cost. Read our review.

8BitDo Ultimate 3E

Where to Buy:

  • $149.99 at Amazon

PlayStation 5 owners looking for a controller upgrade, meanwhile, might consider the DualSense Edge, Sony’s first-party pro-style controller. In addition to a variety of extra function buttons and paddles, the wireless gamepad sports adjustable trigger heights and swappable joysticks (in case the potentiometers start to drift). It’s a little bit heavier than Sony’s regular DualSense, and the battery life isn’t quite as good, but it offers customization you won’t find on the console’s default controller. Read our review.

Sony DualSense Edge

Sony’s pro-style controller, the DualSense Edge, might suffer from shorter battery life than the standard DualSense model, but it features great software integration with the PlayStation 5 and plenty of customizable components.

Where to Buy:

  • $199 $169 at Amazon
  • $199 $169.99 at Best Buy
  • $169 $144 at PlayStation Direct (refurbished)

Charging docks

Nothing’s worse than having to pause a heist so you can go hunt down a fresh set of AA batteries. The PowerA Duo Charging Station includes a rechargeable battery and replacement rear doors for two Xbox Series X / S or Xbox One controllers. Simply set them on the dock, and they’ll start charging.

PowerA Duo Charging Station for Xbox Series X / S

Where to Buy:

  • $29.99 $27.37 at Amazon
  • $32.99 $27.37 at Walmart
  • $32.99 at PowerA

PowerA’s PlayStation equivalent charges two DualSense Wireless Controllers simultaneously, with an included AC adapter, and comes with a two-year warranty.

PowerA Twin Charging Station for DualSense Wireless Controllers

Where to Buy:

  • $27.99 $20.37 at Amazon
  • $27.99 $20.37 at Walmart
  • $27.99 at PowerA

TVs

The 2026 Roku Pro Series is the brand’s first OLED, and the 55-inch version retails for $999.99, which is on the low end of the price spectrum for OLED. Games feel richer and more immersive on OLED panels, thanks to their deeper black levels, which are the result of unlit pixels or sections of the screen. Each Pro Series panel also sports a 120Hz refresh rate, four HDMI 2.1 ports, and both low latency and variable refresh rates for gaming.

Roku Pro Series Smart TV

Where to Buy:

  • $999.99 at Amazon (55-inch)
  • $1199.99 at Amazon (65-inch)

For a more premium offering, the Sony Bravia 8 II is one of our favorite screens for movies, with an engaging, immersive picture and excellent image processing. It has great gaming features, too, like a 120Hz refresh rate with variable refresh and an automatic low-latency mode. It’s not cheap, but the OLED makes for an excellent upgrade to your setup. Read our review.

Sony Bravia 8 II OLED TV

Where to Buy:

  • $3299.99 $2198 at Amazon (65-inch)
  • $3299.99 $2199.99 at Best Buy (65-inch)
  • $3299.99 $2199.99 at Sony (65-inch)

Headsets

Sony’s latest first-party headset, the $99 PlayStation Pulse Wireless, launches the same day as GTA VI. My colleague Cameron Faulkner recently went hands-on with the wireless headset ahead of its launch on November 19th, and came away impressed with its overall audio quality and comfort. The newest Pulse is also straightforward to set up and use, especially when paired with devices like the PlayStation Portal that support PlayStation Link, Sony’s proprietary low-latency audio connection. It also offers Bluetooth for use with other devices.

Sony PlayStation Pulse wireless headset

Where to Buy:

  • $99 at Amazon
  • $99 at PlayStation Store
  • $99.99 at Target

For Xbox gamers, it’s hard to beat the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 3X, which retails in multiple colors for $109.99 or less. The wireless headset is lightweight, comfortable, and compatible with a wide variety of other consoles and mobile devices as well, for those rare moments when you aren’t playing GTA VI.

SteelSeries Arctis Nova 3X

Where to Buy:

  • $109.99 $81.81 at Amazon
  • $109.99 at Best Buy
  • $109.99 $86.99 at SteelSeries

If you’d rather the simplicity of a wired option, Sony’s InZone H6 Air skips the batteries and dongles, instead opting to plug straight into your controller. This open-back gaming headset is lightweight and comfortable, which is great for long hours and late nights. My colleague Cameron Faulkner described its sound as “spectacular,” with several equalizer options available for helping fine-tune the sound to your liking. Read our review.

Sony InZone H6 Air

Where to Buy:

  • $199.99 $168 at Amazon
  • $199.99 $169.99 at Best Buy
  • $199.99 $169.99 at Sony

One additional upgrade

Ikea’s Poäng chair balances affordability and comfort, with wide, supportive armrests that are just the right height for holding a controller. It comes in a variety of frame materials and cushion colors, too, making it easy to match your other furniture or console. This is my personal chair for console gaming, and I recently added a matching ottoman to the set for maximum relaxation.

Ikea Poäng Chair

Where to Buy:

  • $199 at Ikea

item.title: Google is forcing Android app developers to properly support foldables
item.description:
Now that Apple's foldable is here, Google wants to make sure apps on Android foldables are a good experience. Starting in April 2027, Google is going to require Android developers to make sure their apps have a baseline level of support for foldables. If they don't, developers risk not being able to publish or update their apps or have reduced visibility for their apps on Google Play.

Google says Android apps must meet its "Tier 3 - Adaptive ready" standard. "Apps must fill the available display area without letterboxing or compatibility modes," Google says. "Apps must preserve state (scroll position, text input, media playback) during rota …

Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Disney’s new Star Wars animatronics interact with guests using AI
item.description:
As advanced and lifelike as the animatronic characters at Disney parks have become, they typically either stick to predefined movements and routines, or there's an out of sight puppeteer helping make their behavior appear more spontaneous. That could soon change as Walt Disney Imagineering R&D has revealed three new Audio-Animatronic prototypes that rely on Amazon's AWS cloud and AI capabilities to respond in unique ways to guest interactions in real-time.

The three animatronics, named Vilo Vele, Kado Bre'a, and Jibu Bre'a, are based on the Star Wars alien characters called the Anzellans that were featured in The Mandalorian and Grogu film …

It's not a cheap solution, but it's cheaper than the fallout of a leak turning into a disaster.

The Neo Smart Water Valve is designed to be installed on a standard US 1-inch thread connection (the co …

item.title: 8BitDo’s new gamepad modernizes the Nintendo GameCube’s WaveBird
item.description:
The 8BitDo 64 was a loose remake of the Nintendo 64's unusual triple-grip controller that did away with that gamepad's centered analog stick. item.title: Remember the frontier AI pause? Chip companies don’t either
item.description:
This summer, OpenAI paused its largest planned frontier training run after its AI agents accidentally hacked Hugging Face and early evidence suggested that its next model could independently find and exploit security flaws. In September, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing advances in the most powerful AI models, warning that they could be used to launch cyberattacks or become harder for their own creators to control.

It was a strange moment for the AI boom. The people building the most powerful models were warning about what those models might be capable of, and investors were suddenly wondering what would happen to chip demand i …

Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: The Verge’s 2026 holiday gift guide for travelers
item.description:
Everyone has that traveler in their life. That person who feels more at home on a 14-hour train ride than a quiet Sunday on the couch. They speak multiple languages, have a gut like a goat, and make friends wherever they go. Whether they're your kindred spirit or the person you live vicariously through, one thing never changes: They always need new gear.

That's what makes travelers so fun to buy for. But you don't want to get them just anything. The key is to find that clever gift even they didn't know they needed, and that's where we come in. From streaming gadgets for the hotel to portable espresso makers and high-capacity charger …
